title: Peri-lymphatic Healing Approach for Intracranial Drainage in Refractory Amyloid-angiopathy
summary:
Cerebral amyloid angiopathy is a condition in which the protein amyloid-β is deposited in the walls of small and medium-sized brain vessels. These deposits can weaken the vessels, increase the risk of intracerebral haemorrhage and are associated with a progressive decline in memory and cognitive performance. Recent research suggests that the lymphatic vessels of the meninges, which drain into the deep cervical lymph nodes, play an important role in clearing these harmful proteins from the brain.

This study investigates whether a novel operation can improve drainage via these lymphatic pathways. In the procedure, known as CSLUS ("Cervical Shunting to Unclog Lymphatic Systems"), very fine lymphatic vessels in the neck are connected to small adjacent veins under the operating microscope (lymphovenous anastomosis) in order to support drainage from the brain. A total of 30 patients aged 60 years or older with mild to moderate cerebral amyloid angiopathy take part. Random allocation (1:1 randomisation) determines whether a participant receives the operation in addition to usual care (intervention group) or continues standard therapy without surgery (control group). All participants are followed up for twelve months (after one week, four weeks, and after three, six and twelve months). The assessments focus on memory and cognitive performance (MMSE, MoCA, DemTect) as well as quality of life, blood and cerebrospinal fluid parameters and possible complications.

The aim of this pilot study is to determine whether the procedure is feasible and safe and whether it can stabilise or improve cognitive performance. The results are intended to provide the basis for larger follow-up studies.

interventions.name: Intervention group (CSLUS): Supermicrosurgical lymphovenous anastomosis in side-to-end technique between the deep cervical lymphatic vessels and adjacent veins to improve lymphatic drainage from the brain, performed by an experienced plastic surgical team, in addition to unchanged standard therapy.

Control group: Continuation of standard therapy (including existing medication, strict blood pressure control and avoidance of risk-increasing anticoagulant medication) without surgical intervention. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosed cerebral amyloid angiopathy with mild to moderate cognitive impairment (MMSE approx. 15–24)
- Age ≥ 60 years
- Written informed consent of the participant if capable of consenting; in the case of disease-related lack of capacity to consent, written informed consent of the legal representative, provided the requirements for study participation are otherwise met
Exclusion criteria:
- Severe other psychiatric disorders with lack of capacity to consent
- Extensive previous surgery or lymph node dissection in the cervical region rendering the procedure technically unfeasible
- Known allergy or intolerance to materials used during surgery
- Participation in other clinical trials that could bias the results
- Severe multimorbidity (ASA classification > IV)
